chapter: Los Angeles: Roy Milton and Central Avenue
title: Joe Morris' Plantation and the Eckstine band again
summary: The Plantation at 97th and Central, and the Eckstine band's new personnel; Dizzy rehearsing 'Woody 'n You'.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Also, out on the south end, around 97th and Central Avenue, they had a club that played big bands. And that's where I heard Billie Holiday again. It was called the Plantation. The owner's name was Joe Morris; it was called Joe Morris' Plantation. And when Billy Eckstine came to town with his band, that was the first place they played, was at the Plantation.

Around 97th and Central. Yeah, and it was a real pleasure to hear that band. Some of the personnel had changed, and the band had been recorded. They had made "Rhythm In A Riff" with Billy Eckstine, and "Opus X" with John Jackson, the fine lead alto player who was Charlie Parker's protege from Kansas City, who played the solo on

the record. And Fats Navarro had joined the band in Dizzy Gillespie's place. Miles Davis spent some time with the band later on. And the tenor saxophone section now had become Dexter Gordon and Gene Ammons; that was the tenor saxophone section.

And I also heard the band when Ammons first joined it. We crossed up...our band, Ernie Fields' band... We were in Evansville, Indiana at the same time, and Ammons had just joined the band. And I'll never forget, Dizzy was teaching the band "Woody 'n You" before the gig started. You know, they didn't have too much time to rehearse out on the road, so they had to rehearse whenever they could. If they'd get in town early, they were rehearsing right up to the time to play the job. Because they were working on this new thing that Dizzy and Charlie and all of them had going -- this new approach. And it was a real treat to hear that band again, especially with some of this new personnel. And the band had developed, and it was really, really something to hear.
